question.text: Given that $ \| \mathbf{u} \| =4$ and $\mathbf{u} \cdot \mathbf{v}=-16$, find the smallest possible value of $\Vert 2\mathbf{v}\Vert.$
question.explanation:
Using the Cauchy-Schwarz inequality, we have

\begin{align*} \vert \mathbf{u}\cdot \mathbf{v} \vert &\leq \Vert \mathbf{u} \Vert \cdot \Vert \mathbf{v} \Vert \\[5pt] \vert -16 \vert & \leq 4 \cdot \Vert \mathbf{v} \Vert \\[5pt] 4 &\leq \Vert \mathbf{v} \Vert. \end{align*}

Now, we multiply both sides of the inequality by $2\mathbin{:}$

\begin{align*} 2 \cdot 4 &\leq 2 \cdot \Vert \mathbf{v} \Vert \\[3pt] 8 &\leq \Vert 2 \mathbf{v} \Vert \end{align*}

Therefore, the minimum possible value of $\Vert 2\mathbf{v}\Vert$ is $8.$

question.text: Given that $ \| \mathbf{u} \| =5$ and $\mathbf{u} \cdot \mathbf{v}=-30$, find the smallest possible value of $\Vert 3\mathbf{v}\Vert.$
question.explanation:
Using the Cauchy-Schwarz inequality, we have

\begin{align*} \vert \mathbf{u}\cdot \mathbf{v} \vert &\leq \Vert \mathbf{u} \Vert \cdot \Vert \mathbf{v} \Vert \\[5pt] \vert -30 \vert & \leq 5 \cdot \Vert \mathbf{v} \Vert \\[5pt] 6 &\leq \Vert \mathbf{v} \Vert. \end{align*}

Now, we multiply both sides of the inequality by $3\mathbin{:}$

\begin{align*} 3\cdot 6 &\leq 3\cdot \Vert \mathbf{v} \Vert \\[5pt] 18 & \leq \Vert 3\mathbf{v} \Vert \end{align*} Therefore, the smallest possible value of $\Vert 3\mathbf{v}\Vert$ is $18.$

question.text: Given that $\Vert \mathbf{u}\Vert =5$ and $\mathbf{u} \cdot \mathbf{v}=-15$, find the smallest possible value of $\Vert \mathbf{v}\Vert.$
question.explanation:
Using the Cauchy-Schwarz inequality, we have

\begin{align*} \vert \mathbf{u}\cdot \mathbf{v} \vert &\leq \Vert \mathbf{u} \Vert \cdot \Vert \mathbf{v} \Vert \\[5pt] \vert -15 \vert & \leq 5 \cdot \Vert \mathbf{v} \Vert\\[5pt] 15 & \leq 5 \cdot \Vert \mathbf{v} \Vert. \end{align*}

Now, we multiply both sides of the inequality by $\dfrac15\mathbin{:}$

\begin{align*} \dfrac15\cdot 15 & \leq \dfrac15 \cdot 5\cdot \Vert \mathbf{v} \Vert\\[5pt] 3 & \leq \Vert \mathbf{v} \Vert \end{align*}

Therefore, the smallest possible value of $\Vert \mathbf{v}\Vert$ is $3.$
